name: France
deceptionLabel: The 20-22% Hidden Employee SSC + 36-40% Employer Contributions
note: Headline income tax brackets look moderate (0/11/30/41/45%), but employee SSC adds ~20%, then employer pays another 36-40% on top of gross — all mostly uncapped.

layers.label: Income Tax (Impôt sur le Revenu)
layers.taxableIncomeNote: Pass 1 simplified base: gross * 0.90 (10% professional deduction), capped deduction at €14,426. Pass 2 base: gross - deductible SSC - professional deduction.

layers.label: Old-Age Pension — Capped (Assurance Vieillesse Plafonnée)
layers.note: 6.9% only up to PASS (€47,100). Above that, stops — most impactful for mid salaries.

layers.label: Old-Age Pension — Uncapped (Assurance Vieillesse Déplafonnée)
layers.note: 0.4% on ALL salary, no ceiling whatsoever.

layers.label: Unemployment Insurance (Assurance Chômage)
layers.note: 2.4% up to 4x PASS. Effectively uncapped for any realistic salary.

layers.label: Supplementary Pension T2 — AGIRC-ARRCO
layers.note: 8.64% on salary between PASS and 8x PASS. For a €65K salary this applies to ~€17,900.

layers.label: General Equilibrium Contribution T2 (CEG)
layers.note: 1.08% on salary between PASS and 8x PASS.

layers.label: CSG — Deductible Portion
layers.note: 6.8% x 98.25% of gross (up to 4x PASS, then 100% of gross above). This portion IS deductible from income tax — reduces your taxable base.

layers.label: CSG — Non-Deductible Portion 😈
layers.note: 2.4% x 98.25% of gross. NOT deductible — sits inside your income tax base. This is a key hidden layer.

layers.label: Social Debt Repayment (CRDS) 😈
layers.note: 0.5% x 98.25% of gross. Also NOT deductible for income tax.

layers.label: Health Insurance — Employer (Assurance Maladie) 💀
layers.note: ~13% on ALL salary, no cap. Largest single employer contribution. Reduced to ~7% for very low salaries only.

layers.label: Employer Pension Overflow (Assurance Vieillesse Déplafonnée)
layers.note: 2.02% on ALL salary above PASS — no upper cap. Pension contributions never fully stop.

layers.label: Family Allowances (Allocations Familiales)
layers.note: Jumps from 3.45% to 5.25% once salary crosses 3.5x SMIC (~€75,677) AND applies retroactively to full salary — creates a small cliff effect.

layers.label: Unemployment Insurance — Employer
layers.note: 4.05% up to 4x PASS. Blended ~4.025% for 2025 (4.05% Jan-Apr, 4.00% May-Dec).

layers.label: AGIRC-ARRCO Supplementary Pension T2 — Employer
layers.note: 12.95% from PASS to 8x PASS. Largest single tier rate of any employer contribution.

layers.label: Work Accident & Occupational Disease Insurance
layers.note: ~0.77% average for office/tech. Sector-variable — set annually per company risk profile. Cannot be modeled exactly without sector.

layers.label: Wage Guarantee Fund (AGS)
layers.note: 0.25% on all salary. Guarantees wages if company becomes insolvent.

calculationNotes.deductibleSSC: pension_capped + pension_uncapped + unemployment + agirc_t1 + agirc_t2 + ceg_t1 + ceg_t2 + csg_deductible
calculationNotes.importantEffect: Moving from pass1 to pass2: income tax DECREASES (larger deductions reduce taxable base) but total burden INCREASES significantly due to SSC. This is a key visual moment.
